analysis: Wallemberg syndrome, also known as lateral medullary syndrome, typically presents with a cluster of symptoms due to ischemia in the dorsolateral region of the medulla oblongata. The symptoms include dysphagia, ataxia, Horner syndrome, and ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature sensation in the face and contralateral loss in the body. Pyramidal signs are not typically associated with Wallemberg syndrome.
